name: Edikang Ikong
summary: A generous vegetable soup of fluted pumpkin and waterleaf with palm oil, periwinkles, meats and dried fish.
story: Edikang ikong comes from the Efik and Ibibio people of south-eastern Nigeria and is well known for its large quantity of leaves. It is often served at weddings and special meals. It is usually eaten with a swallow such as fufu, garri or pounded yam.

steps.title: Cook the meats
steps.text: Boil the meat with onion, stock cubes and salt until tender, adding stockfish near the end. Reserve about 1 cup of stock.

steps.title: Prepare greens
steps.text: Slice the ugu thinly and chop the waterleaf. Squeeze the waterleaf lightly to remove excess water.

steps.title: Start with palm oil
steps.text: In a wide pot warm the palm oil briefly, add the onion and pepper, and cook for 2 to 3 minutes. Add the crayfish, periwinkles and meats with a little stock.

steps.title: Add waterleaf
steps.text: Add the waterleaf first and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until it wilts and releases juice, which becomes the soup liquid.

steps.title: Add the pumpkin leaves
steps.text: Stir in the ugu, cover for 3 minutes, then stir again. Cook for 5 to 8 minutes in total until the leaves are tender but still green.

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.text: Taste and adjust salt. The soup should be thick with greens, glistening with palm oil and not watery.

tips: Do not add much water; the waterleaf supplies the liquid.
Cook ugu briefly to keep colour and a little bite.
Use plenty of greens, since they cook down a lot.

swaps.swap: Spinach, kale or chard are the usual substitutes abroad; kale needs a few more minutes.
Baby spinach with a splash of stock.
Omit or add a handful of small clams or shrimp.
